title: LookTerrain
description: Data file content/look/terrain.json: how the island grid is drawn (B2 R18-R20): palette colours per biome, for cliffs and the ground under water, the water surfaces and the detail levels of the chunks. Ids refer to content/look/palette.json. Presentation only, not part of the hash. Values are placeholders.

biome_colors.description: Ground colour of each biome (biome id from content/world/biomes.json, colour id from the palette).

bed_color.description: Palette colour of the ground under water.

slope_shade_permille.description: How much steep ground is darkened towards the cliff colour (0 = not at all, 1000 = fully).

slope_shade_gain.description: How fast slope shading rises with steepness: (1 - normal.y) times this, capped at 1, then scaled by slope_shade_permille.

open_sea_size_factor.description: Size of the open sea plane around the map, as a multiple of the map's width and depth.

tide_follow_real_seconds.description: Optional: time constant in real seconds with which the drawn sea surface follows the tide level of the core (B2-5 R15), so the water glides at every game speed. Missing or 0 = the surface shows every level at once.

water_time_wrap_seconds.description: Period of the water clock in real seconds (W1724): the time flow lines, shimmer, foam and wave crests move by runs only while the game is not paused and starts again after this long. Every cycle of the water shaders is rounded to a whole number of rounds per period (at least one) and every scrolling pattern repeats after the steps it scrolls per period, so the wrap does not show - with any period; a short one (10) is the quick way to look for a jump, it only makes slow cycles run faster. Absent = 3600.

TerrainRock.description: Natural rock (TL #19984): colour variation on the cliff biomes' ground and walls, darker wall feet, and scree tint on the ground at the foot of a wall, so rock does not read as one flat grey. Absent = plain colours.

variation_permille.description: Largest brightness change of rock ground and walls (permille, both ways), from a smooth noise over the grid.

variation_cells.description: Size of the colour patches (noise wavelength in cells).

wall_foot_shade_permille.description: How much darker a wall is at its foot than at its top edge (permille).

scree_permille.description: How far the ground colour at the foot of a wall leans towards the rock colour (permille), so rock and grass blend.

TerrainCliffs.description: Where the ground is drawn as a vertical rock wall instead of a slope (D576, TL #19553): only between two neighbouring cells whose heights differ by at least min_drop_mm and whose higher cell belongs to one of these biomes. Everywhere else the corner heights blend across the drop, so hills and terraces are smooth slopes. Placeholder values.

biomes.description: Biome ids (content/world/biomes.json) whose cells form rock walls where they stand above a neighbour.

min_drop_mm.description: Smallest height difference (millimetres) between neighbouring cells that becomes a rock wall.

TerrainWater.description: Palette colours of the water surfaces and the depth (in height units) from which water counts as deep.

swamp_max_units.description: Fresh water this shallow (height units) is drawn as murky swamp.

stream_shore_lift_mm.description: Where a stream borders dry ground its edge comes down to the ground and lies this far above it (millimetres), so the edge closes against the bank without flickering into it.

stream_width_m.description: Width of a stream band in metres: streams are drawn as smooth bands along their centre line (A1456); the generator makes them two cells wide.

stream_smoothing.description: Rounds of corner cutting (Chaikin) along a stream's centre line, after the relaxing; each round doubles the points (0 = the relaxed cell-centre polyline).

stream_source_taper_m.description: Length over which a stream widens from its source (a spring seep) to its full width, in metres.

stream_source_width_share.description: Width of a stream at its source as a share of its full width (0..1); it widens over stream_source_taper_m.

stream_relax_passes.description: Most smoothing passes over a stream's centre line before the corner cutting (W1724): each pass moves every point halfway to the middle of its neighbours, the ends stay. The relaxing stops earlier once the line turns no more than stream_turn_goal_deg_per_m. Absent or 0 = none.

stream_turn_goal_deg_per_m.description: Turn of a stream's centre line in degrees per metre (the angle between the metre before a place and the metre after it) the relaxing aims at: it goes on until the line is this smooth or the passes are used up. Absent = every pass is used.

stream_max_turn_deg_per_m.description: Largest turn of a drawn stream line in degrees per metre: where the cells of a stream do not let the relaxing reach its goal (a hairpin), the line may turn up to this. The tests hold the streams of the real islands to it. Absent = no promise.

stream_cell_tolerance_m.description: How far the smoothed centre line may leave the stream's own cells, in metres; a point that would go further is held back. Absent = 0.25.

stream_max_shift_m.description: How far the relaxing may move a point of the centre line from where the cells put it, in metres. Absent = 0.5.

stream_cover_m.description: Every cell of a stream keeps the relaxed centre line within this distance of its centre, in metres: where a stream is several cells wide a point may move less, so no cut bed is left without its band. Absent = 1.2.

swamp_as_ground.description: Swamp water (fresh water no deeper than swamp_max_units) is drawn as wet ground in the swamp colour, blended into the ground around it like a biome border, instead of as a water plate with a hard edge along the cells (W1724). Absent = false.

TerrainStreamMouth.description: How a stream band ends in standing water (TL #20750, W1738). At the sea the band thins out to a film on the ground before the coast and runs on over the beach the low tide leaves dry, down to the low-tide line, where it ends under the lowest water; the sea surface, which follows the tide, covers whatever lies below it, so the stream ends at the waterline at every tide. In a lake the band never lies above the lake's surface. Absent = the band ends in the first cell of standing water as before.

fade_m.description: Length in metres before the coast over which the water of a stream that runs into the sea thins from its depth to a film on the ground (the height of stream_shore_lift_mm), so it meets the beach without a step.

reach_cells.description: Most sea cells a stream runs on over, down the sea floor, to reach ground that lies under the lowest tide.

under_mm.description: How far below the receiving water the band ends, in millimetres: below the lowest tide at the sea, below the surface in a lake.

widen_share.description: How much wider the band is at its end in the sea than at the coast, as a share of its width (0 = it keeps its width): the stream fans out over the beach.

TerrainWaterShader.description: Parameters of the fresh water shader (game/shaders/island_water.gdshader): light flow lines that drift down a stream, each lane at its own pace (W1724), and a slow shimmer on still water.

flow_lanes.description: Lanes of flow lines across a stream band.

flow_line_length_m.description: Typical length of a flow line along the stream in metres.

flow_speed_m_per_s.description: Mean speed the flow lines drift downstream, metres per second.

flow_speed_spread.description: How much the speed differs from lane to lane (0 = all the same, 1 = from half to one and a half times the mean).

flow_bend.description: How far the lanes wander sideways along the stream, in lane widths.

shimmer_speed.description: Speed of the shimmer on still water.

TerrainDetail.description: Detail levels of the terrain chunks (B2 R18): each chunk has one ground mesh per level, built once from the base grid (it never changes at run time). A coarser level merges blocks of plain dry land into a few triangles within its tolerances and draws coast, banks, water and cliffs as the base grid does; the water is always drawn from the base grid. Godot switches between the levels by the camera distance to the chunk (visibility ranges, switched at until_m without fade, with a small hysteresis: the levels share their borders and differ only within the tolerances) and culls chunks outside the view.

levels.description: Levels from near to far: the first has cell_step 1 (the base grid); cell steps rise, each a divisor of the chunk size; every level but the last ends at until_m (rising), the last reaches to the horizon; coarser levels need max_error_mm and max_color_delta_permille.

sea_floor_margin_mm.description: Coarser levels merge open sea bed only where every merged corner lies at least this far (millimetres) below the sea surface, so the floor never shows through or flickers with the water.

switch_margin_m.description: Hysteresis of the switch between two levels (metres): a shown level stays up to twice this beyond until_m, so chunks do not pop back and forth while the camera eases; a hidden one appears exactly at until_m. Levels must lie more than four margins apart.

cell_step.description: Edge length in grid cells of the blocks this level may merge (1 = every cell of the base grid).

until_m.description: Camera distance to the chunk (metres) up to which this level is drawn; missing on the last level.

max_error_mm.description: Largest height difference (millimetres) of a merged block from the base grid; blocks that would differ more stay at full detail.

max_color_delta_permille.description: Largest colour difference per channel (permille) of a merged block from the base grid; blocks that would differ more stay at full detail.

TerrainWaves.description: Wave crests on the sea and on lakes (W1724, game/shaders/water_waves.gdshaderinc): light bowed strokes that travel with the wind. How many there are comes from the weather (content/look/weather.json, waves 0..1): none, a few small ones, many large ones. Absent = no crests.

strength.description: How strongly a crest lightens the water (0..1).

lake_share.description: Share of the weather's waves a lake shows (lakes are calmer than the sea).

shore_foam_gain.description: How much wider the foam line at the shore breathes in full waves (0 = unchanged, 1 = twice).

turn_real_seconds.description: Real seconds over which the crests follow a turned wind: their strokes turn in place and their path bends, nothing slides or reshuffles. Absent = 4.

TerrainWaveLayer.description: One layer of wave crests on a square grid that is fixed in the world and never turns; the wind only pushes the grid along (the game sums up direction times speed times time). The weather only decides how many of its places carry a crest, so neither a change of weather nor a turning wind ever moves a crest out of its place.

spacing_m.description: Size of one place of the crest grid in metres (the distance between two crests).

length_m.description: Longest crest in metres (at most two thirds of spacing_m is drawn, so a crest fits its place whichever way the wind turns it).

thickness_m.description: Thickness of a crest stroke in metres (at most 8 percent of spacing_m is drawn).

speed_m_per_s.description: Speed the crests travel with the wind, metres per second.

density.description: Share of the places that carry a crest when the layer is full (0..1).

starts_at.description: Waves value (0..1) at which the first crests of this layer appear.

full_at.description: Waves value (0..1) from which the layer is full; must lie above starts_at.
